narrative: The model estimated a 58% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning it judged the chance of repayment problems to be slightly higher than the chance of successful repayment; on that basis, the application was denied. The strongest single reason was the size of the loan you requested. You asked for 13,756 DM over 60 months, whereas approved applicants requested about 3,020 DM on average and typically borrowed for around 19 months. This unusually large and long commitment was the leading factor pushing the decision toward bad credit. Your checking account status ranked second in influence, but it worked in your favor, pushing toward good credit; having no recorded checking account status is common among approved applicants. Your savings information ranked third and also helped your case, moving the assessment toward good credit; having unknown or no savings was not unusual in the approved group. In other words, two of the most important factors supported you, but they were not enough to overcome the concern created by the requested loan size. Next, consider applying for a substantially smaller amount and a shorter repayment period, and provide clear statements for your checking and savings accounts. You could also ask the bank what monthly repayment level it considers affordable, or consider a guarantor or co-applicant to strengthen a future application.
